text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options softened from Monday's lofty levels, while those for dollar/yen were well bid, particularly the one-month maturity, U.S. traders said.

Although spot dollar/yen drifted in familiar ranges around 116 yen and volatilities initially dipped in early Asian trade, several big U.S. investment banks began bidding for options aggressively from European time-zone, dealers said.
Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank in New York, noted that the focus was on one-month options as those traded between Monday and Wednesday expire on July 3.
That meant the options would cover the June 20-22 Group of Seven summit, the Bank of Japan's "tankan" report due June 25 and the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting July 1-2.
In addition, the July 3 expiries would avoid the time-decay for the long U.S. Independence Day weekend.

"One-month really stands out," Okada said. "This inversion is different from the one a few weeks ago that was caused by the dollar's plunge in that one- and two- weeks are below one-month. It seems people are expecting spot to be stagnant in the very near term and want to trim some time-decay out of that one-month exposure."

One-month dollar/yen implied volatility stood at 10.6/10.8 pecent in mid-afternoon U.S., up from early Asian lows below 10 and 10.3/10.5 late on Monday. Two-month and out were generally 0.1-0.2 point higher at about 10.0/10.2 percent.

Traders said the back months had been depressed on Monday due to excess vega in the market after a dollar-bullish Japanese insurance firm sold a total of some $1 billion of six-month yen calls with a knockout barrier at 125 yen.
Still, risk-reversals, the put/call pricing differential, remained heavily slanted in favor of yen calls. One-month 25-delta stood at 1.0/1.2 point skewed for yen calls.

In dollar/mark, volatilities eased as spot drifted in the upper-1.72 mark area. The pause weighed on the gamma-rich front end, which had spiked up on Monday when the greenback gapped up nearly three pfennigs to above 1.73 marks.
One-month dollar/mark was half a point lower at 9.8/10.0 percent, while one-month was off about 0.1 at 9.55/9.75.
Alan Revercomb, options strategist at I.D.E.A. Inc, said mark/yen options looked attractive as spot dollar/mark faded.
"That's been the consistent money-making gamma," he said. "On an intraday basis, mark/yen actuals (historical volatilities) are above dollar/mark and dollar/yen's."
"One-month actuals are still up in the teens, so you've got a reasonable discount there," he said. One-month mark/yen implied was at 10.4/10.7 percent.
You also have that (discount) in the other pairs, but the difference seems to be mark/yen is not really decelerating. It's been moved by one or the other (mark or yen)."

"Mark/yen gamma doesn't tend to be profitable for that long because usually it turns out to be a dollar move in one direction or the other, but this just hasn't occurred," he said. One-month dollar/mark risk reversal was at 0.2/0.5 point for mark puts, in contrast to the yen-call skew in dollar/yen.
